title: Enhancing academic writing skills and motivation: assessing the efficacy of ChatGPT in AI-assisted language learning for EFL students
extended_summary:
This mixed-methods study examines whether AI-assisted language learning using ChatGPT can improve EFL students’ academic writing skills and writing motivation. The paper is motivated by the challenge of providing timely, detailed writing feedback and the need to understand how AI tools might supplement or outperform traditional instruction in language learning.

The intervention compared ChatGPT-based writing support with traditional teacher-led writing instruction. Fifty Chinese undergraduate EFL students at a national university were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group. Over a 12-week period, both groups completed similar writing tasks in the same university setting, with the experimental group receiving real-time AI feedback on grammar, vocabulary, organization, coherence, and sentence structure, while the control group received teacher feedback. The study used pre/post IELTS academic writing tasks, a writing motivation questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews with a subset of students.

Results showed that students using ChatGPT improved more than the control group in overall writing performance, as well as in content, organization, language use, and motivation. The qualitative interviews suggested that students found the AI feedback innovative, convenient, and helpful for revision, though some expressed concerns about over-reliance and contextual accuracy. Overall, the paper concludes that ChatGPT can be an effective scaffold for academic writing and motivation in EFL contexts, while noting the importance of ethical and guided use.

The findings are specific to a small sample of Chinese undergraduates in one university and reflect short-term outcomes measured immediately after the intervention.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed randomized controlled pre-test/post-test study with a comparison group, which supports causal inference. However, it is a small single-site study (n=50) in higher education EFL rather than K-12, and the intervention/comparator context is narrower than ideal for full blue-tier confidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports medium-to-large positive effects on writing outcomes and motivation (e.g., d=0.52 to 0.88; partial eta squared up to 0.38), indicating practically meaningful impact. Because the evidence comes from a small non-K-12 sample and focuses on writing rather than the requested science inquiry context, the broader generalizable impact remains modest rather than blue-tier.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as an AI-assisted writing tutor providing real-time conversational feedback, suggestions, and explanations for EFL academic writing across grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and organization.
ChatGPT used as an AI writing support tool for EFL students to revise academic writing drafts, correct language errors, and improve writing quality and motivation.

finding.finding_summary: The AI-assisted ChatGPT group outperformed the traditional instruction group on overall academic writing performance after 12 weeks (n=50). Post-test overall writing scores were higher in the experimental group (M=59.12, SD=14.23) than the control group (M=45.18, SD=15.62), with t(48)=3.79, p<0.001 and Cohen’s d=0.76. ANCOVA also showed a significant group effect on global writing, F(1,47)=19.01, partial eta squared=0.27.
finding.measure: IELTS academic writing tasks 1 and 2 scored with IELTS band descriptors; overall writing performance

finding.finding_summary: Writing motivation improved more in the ChatGPT group than in the traditional instruction group over the 12-week intervention (n=50). Post-test motivation scores were higher for the experimental group (M=20.06, SD=3.33) than the control group (M=18.21, SD=3.58), with t(48)=3.34, p=0.001 and Cohen’s d=0.52. ANCOVA also found a significant group effect on writing motivation, F(1,47)=29.62, partial eta squared=0.38.

The ChatGPT group showed significant gains in writing content relative to the control group after instruction (n=50). Post-test content scores were higher in the experimental group (M=15.96, SD=3.71) than the control group (M=13.71, SD=3.12), with t(48)=3.01, p=0.003 and Cohen’s d=0.65. The authors also report a significant ANCOVA group effect for writing content, F(1,47)=12.61, p=0.00, partial eta squared=0.19.

The ChatGPT intervention produced stronger improvement in writing organization than traditional instruction (n=50). Post-test organization scores were higher in the experimental group (M=16.56, SD=3.54) than the control group (M=13.63, SD=3.63), with t(48)=4.12, p<0.001 and Cohen’s d=0.84. ANCOVA confirmed a significant group effect, F(1,47)=23.16, p=0.00, partial eta squared=0.34.

ChatGPT-based instruction also improved language use more than conventional instruction (n=50). Post-test language use scores were higher in the experimental group (M=19.89, SD=4.82) than the control group (M=15.89, SD=4.12), with t(48)=4.34, p<0.001 and Cohen’s d=0.88. The ANCOVA likewise indicated a significant group difference, F(1,47)=9.86, p=0.01, partial eta squared=0.11.
